The last FIFA I played was FIFA 12 and I had no interest in FUT back then. I picked this FIFA up just to see the FUT experience for the first time. I grinded to Elite division very quickly also got rank 1 in the old FUT Champions system. To be honest my experience started off very good, the game was very fluid. 

It all started on Black Friday and that time I realised what I got into. EA started bursting out packs non-stop. Until that point I felt like the pack system was okay and fair but after Black Friday I saw what FUT really is about. Nonstop gamble + the pressure of FOMO. Luckily I'm not a huge gambler and I don't believe in spending fortune on an RNG. Paid content like battle passes or quality of life upgrades are fair in games, but paying money for RNG is nothing different than going to a casino and playing slot machines.

After the Fire/Freeze promo I also started experiencing the muddy gameplay where your players start feeling like bronze players. This still happens almost %20-30 of the time. Happens a lot on Fridays when Fut champions start, or a new promo gets released. Btw according to EA my connection quality is 99/100 and I have 500/500mbit fibre. There was a huge forum thread about this in the EA forums and they never did anything to fix it. I then found out that this was an ongoing problem that happens in almost every FUT season.

One good thing about FUT is that it definitely rewards you if you grind the game. A lot of usable SBC players, couple of squad foundation players, and also a lot of packs are given by the game, if you do the achievements and objectives.

Overall though, when you get to a certain point, the only thing that keeps you in the game is that moment when you pack a really really good meta player, which never happens because it's like one in a million chance. I can guarantee that it will not happen to you either unless you are a very very very very lucky person. Gameplay becomes boring when you get into it. Some basic skill moves, ball roll, driven passes, left stick dribble with lean/unique high agility players, green timed shots and that's it, you're in elite division and get to at least rank 3 in the new FUT champs system.

EA constantly puts out promos and boost the stats of same players over and over again, If you want to keep up with the game but if you don't want to spend money on promos that will go to waste when Fifa 23 comes out, I suggest you don't buy this game and don't invest your precious time.

All the time I put in this game will disappear when the new one comes out. All the money that people spent is also gonna disappear when the new one comes out. Same players over and over, getting their stats boosted +1 every month, until all the cards hit 99.

Stay away and save your time.

After playing over 2,000 hours of this game, split between me and my girlfriend this game feels like a big downgrade from all previous FIFA with many problems I can list. The player switching into the wrong player, clearly when I don't want to switch to that player to the passing detection in this game. In previous FIFAs I've never had an issue with the passing, but in this one my players was making much more passing mistakes than normal. The passing detection shows me that I'm passing to the player that I want but suddenly it switches and passes to a completely different player. 
The game feels too scripty when facing against AI, especially squad battles in FUT. Somehow playing legendary difficulty against bronze team with my full team of special cards and their bronze players can easily keep up with mine. Difficulty shouldn't secretly boost their stats (especially when its on ultimate boosting it to 99), but rather boost the AI intelligence. I've seen some "scripty" moments like when my player is clearly beating the AI when chasing the ball but suddenly my player massively reduce his speed for the AI to get the ball before me. Why does the AI deserve the ball more than me? It should be equally based. The AI can be very sticky with the ball too, like the ball is magnetic to their feet even after clearly tackling them and winning the ball. You can clearly see moments when AI just has to score and you can't do anything about it. I also think the difficulty jump between world class to legendary to ultimate is too big of a gap... there really should be an inbetween difficulty between them. There's moments where I can beat AI on world class like 12-0 then legendary/ultimate I'll be losing 4-0 sometimes. 
Another issue I have is the friendlies in FUT. I'm surprised that there isn't skill-based matchmaking. Sometimes they pair you against someone that is just on another level to you giving you no chance to win. I really think there should be a skill-based matchmaking in this game. 
Career mode can be really buggy, especially showing wrong texts etc.
There's a lot to fix in this game, and hopefully EA can actually be bothered fixing it in the future.

Pros:

- Game has the ideal pace

- Passing rarely goes around players to avoid interceptions, stupid passes are punished

- Both offensive and defensive AI is excellent

- Shot blocking is realistic, no more superman blocks

- Defending is manual enough

- Dribbling is realistic and has quite the skill gap

- Skill moves are about as effective as IRL

- Speed-wise, the attackers/defenders balance is spot on

- Heading is great: still manual, great skill gap, well implemented RNG when heading from difficult spots

Cons:

- Because of the pace, games should be more than 12 mins, and now that you need to play less games on competitive, it's the ideal time to do it

- Tackling is still a bit too easy, should have to be better timed.

- Passing that is not around players is still too easy, you can ping pong around to keep posession too easily

- Through balls on Semi is nowhere near enough to prevent easy counter-attacks, you still don't have to be precise to get good through ball passes. Should be manual like heading.

- Shooting, especially from long range is also too easy

- Goalkeepers are for the most part quite OP to make up for the point above

- Refereeing is still very hit and miss



All in all, this is the best FIFA gameplay ever. Still far from what it could and should be, and that's mostly due to EA's reluctance to remove assists. Remove assisting from shooting like heading, and there's 0 need for superman goalkeepers + you add an actual skill gap in shooting. Also fixes long shots being too easy. That and through balls aswell, just way too easy and they encourage an unnatural amount of parking the bus, as counter-attacking becomes too easy.

Where to begin with FIFA 22? It’s as if the developers decided to take everything that could have possibly been loved about the FIFA franchise, throw it into a blender, and then pour the mixture into a server that's perpetually on fire. If you're seeking the thrill of football, you're better off knitting socks for your local Sunday league team than enduring this travesty.

The game’s ‘innovative’ HyperMotion Technology could have been revolutionary, but instead, it seems to have been designed by someone whose only prior experience with football was a half-remembered PE class from two decades ago. Players on the pitch handle like a supermarket trolley with a busted wheel, veering wildly and rarely going where you want them to.

Ultimate Team? More like the Ultimate Ponzi scheme. The mode is an insidious ploy to pickpocket players under the guise of entertainment, dangling the carrot of elite players in front of us, only to beat us with the stick of reality when we inevitably pull yet another no-name player from a pack.

But let’s talk about the online experience, shall we? The servers are as reliable as a chocolate teapot. You’ll find yourself disconnected from matches with such frequency that you start to wonder if 'server stability' is just a myth EA Sports made up to tease us. And when you are connected, the lag is so bad it feels like your team is playing in treacle - treacle that's past its sell-by date.

The ball physics are an enigma, defying the very essence of gravity and momentum. The ball floats like a balloon on a breezy day, making every attempt at a pass or shot a game of lottery. And tackling? The referees must be using a rulebook from an alternate universe where contact is a sin because you’ll be penalized for so much as breathing too heavily on an opponent.

Career mode remains a neglected wasteland, where the AI transfers and managerial decisions are about as logical as a cat’s strategy in a game of chess. And don’t get me started on the commentary, which has all the variety and excitement of a two-day seminar on watching paint dry.

In essence, FIFA 22 is an overpriced, underperforming shadow of what a football game could and should be. It's a soul-sucking, wallet-emptying husk that masquerades as entertainment. So, if you value your money, time, and love for football, steer clear of this digital doppelgänger of despair.

If you thought the PC community was angry about FIFA 21, FIFA 22 took that frustration and amplified it. Despite PC hardware being more than capable, EA once again decided to treat PC players as an afterthought, delivering the old-generation version of the game while hyping up their new HyperMotion technology exclusively for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series consoles.

Let that sink in: if you bought this on Steam, you were paying full price for a game that was intentionally missing the biggest marketing feature of the year. It was essentially FIFA 21.5 with updated kits and rosters, making the PC player base feel completely disrespected.

As for the actual gameplay we got on PC, it was a very strange mixed bag. The goalkeepers were buffed to an absurd level inside the penalty box, making point-blank saves look like scenes from an action movie. Yet, ironically, you could score finesse shots from 30 yards out with incredible ease. The pace-abuse meta was slightly toned down compared to the previous year, giving passers a bit more room to breathe, but the notorious momentum shifts and heavy scripting were still glaringly present.

 Competitive matches often felt like they were decided by the game engine rather than pure skill.

For offline players, Career Mode introduced the Create a Club feature. It was a step in the right direction and fun for a few seasons, allowing you to design your own kits and stadium, but it ultimately lacked the deep, immersive customization needed to keep it engaging long-term. 

Ultimate Team, as expected, remained the primary focus of the developers, continuing its aggressive trend of heavy monetization and pay-to-win mechanics disguised behind shiny weekly promos.

Objectively speaking, looking at the overwhelming community consensus, it was a deeply disappointing port for the PC platform. It functions as a decent football game if you just want to kick a ball around offline or play locally with friends, but the decision to deny PC players the next-gen engine completely ruined the reputation of this specific release.

Graphics and Presentation:
Visually, FIFA 22 impresses with stunning player models, realistic stadiums, and dynamic weather effects that enhance the immersion. The attention to detail is evident throughout the game, from the grass on the pitch to the facial expressions of the players.

Verdict:
FIFA 22 builds upon the solid foundation of its predecessors, delivering an engaging football experience that will satisfy both casual fans and die-hard enthusiasts. With its refined gameplay, expanded modes, and impressive presentation, FIFA 22 continues to be the go-to choice for football gaming enthusiasts. Whether you're a seasoned veteran or a newcomer to the franchise, FIFA 22 offers something for everyone, making it a must-have for any football fan's collection.
